sentences.text: The Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred to as DAR) was filed in this case on 10.04.2015, with reference to FIR No. 840/14, U/s 279/337 IPC, PS South Rohini, Delhi, in respect of simple hurt, sustained by the petitioner Chand Singh, in a road traffic accident, on 10.09.2014, at about 9.45 pm, inside Depot Rohini III, near CNG Pump, Sector-3, Rohini, Delhi.

Subsequently,
chargesheet was filed against the driver Subhash Kumar (hereinafter referred to as 'Respondent no.1/R1/driver), for the commission of offence U/s 279/337 IPC and Section 3/181 of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V.Act),
as R1 failed to produce his driving license.

The Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal, vide order dated 10.04.2015, treated the DAR, as claim petition U/s 166(4) of M.V.Act.
2.

Brief facts of the case, as discernible from the DAR, including the documents annexed with DAR,

bearing registration no. DL-1PC-8612 (hereinafter referred to as the the offending vehicle), which was driven in a rash and negligent manner, by its driver/R1, inside Rohini Depot III, Delhi.
It was further alleged that while the bus was coming towards him, the petitioner has given signal to R1, to stop the offending vehicle, but R1 failed to stop the vehicle and hit the petitioner.

It was further averred that after hitting the petitioner, R1 stopped the offending vehicle, got down from the same and tried to run away from the spot but, he was apprehended by some of the colleagues of the petitioner, who had also made call at 100 number.
It was further averred that R1 disclosed his name as Subhash, and he also disclosed that he was working as Mechanic, in the said DTC depot.

It was further averred that as a result of the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries, after which, he was taken to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as Mahavir Hospital), in CATS Ambulance, where he was medically examined, vide MLC No. 3903/14,
as per which, injuries sustained by the petitioner was opined to be simple in nature.

3. As per DAR, at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was driven by R1, the same was registered in the name Delhi Transport Corporation (hereinafter referred as DTC/owner of the offending vehicle/respondent no.2/R2) and was insured with United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
(hereinafter referred as insurance company/R3), vide Policy No. 0411003114P100943082, valid for the period 06.05.2014 to 05.05.2015.
4. R1 though appeared at the time of filing of DAR, but, he has chosen not to file any written statement to the DAR/claim petition.

It was further stated that DTC has given maintenance contract to M/s Ashok Leyland and Ashok Leyland has engaged the services of sub-contractor TVS company, for maintenance of DTC buses.
It was further stated that the driver Subhash was not an employee of DTC and he has never been authorized by DTC, to drive the bus, in any manner, whatsoever.

Though, during the course of cross examination of PW1, a suggestion was put to PW1, that the case accident occurred, due to his negligence but, PW1 denied the said suggestion.
Nevertheless, during the course of his cross- examination by Ld. Counsel for R3, PW1 denied the suggestion, that after the accident, he was paid Rs. 14,000/-, by R1.

Rather,
PW1 deposed that in the criminal case, bearing FIR No. 840/14, PS South Rohini, Section 338 IPC has been compounded and there, he has received Rs. 10,500/- from R1.
By putting the said suggestion, R3 admitted that a settlement has been arrived at, between the petitioner and R1, as a result of which, Section 338 IPC was compounded.

Thus, by entering into settlement, with the petitioner, R1 has admitted before the Court of Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate, that the petitioner has sustained injuries, due to his rash and negligent driving.
Therefore, R3 cannot be permitted to deny the aspect of rashness or negligence, on the part of R1, in driving the offending vehicle, resulting in the case accident.

21. Even otherwise, since R1 failed to file any written statement and also failed to cross-examine PW1, despite being granted opportunity therefore, before this Tribunal also, R1 deemed to have admitted that there was rashness and negligence on his part, in causing the accident in question.
Further, R1 also failed to prove that he has ever approached to any higher authority, with respect to his false implication in the present case.

Consequently, in view of the unrebutted testimony of PW1,
it stands duly proved, that the accident, in which the petitioner has sustained injuries, as evident from his MLC and treatment papers, has taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

R3 failed to impeach the veracity of the said bills and failed to disprove the said bills.
Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate, to award compensation of Rs.23,275.40/-, to the petitioner, under the head of medical expenses.
SPECIAL DIET AND CONVEYANCE 25.

The petitioner had sought compensation of Rs. 30,000/-
each, on account of the expenditure incurred by him, on special diet and conveyance.

But, he failed to place on record any prescription slip, of a doctor, medical practitioner or dietitian, issued in his name (the name of the petitioner), advising him to take any form of special diet or any bill of special diet, such as high protein diet or liquid diet or nutritional supplements, for speedy recovery of the injuries sustained in the case accident.

26. Further, he has also not placed on record, any bill of conveyance, such as bills raised by any private taxi service or ambulance service, availed by him for travelling to the hospital from his residence or vice versa, during his treatment period.

In such circumstances, the requirement of special diet and conveyance, if any faced by the petitioner, during his treatment period, has to be ascertained, in accordance with the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner.

27. In this context, perusal of the record reveals that after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura, Delhi, in CATS Ambulance, where he was medically examined, vide MLC No. 3903/14, as per which, injuries sustained by him, was opined to be simple in nature.
But, on 11.09.2014, the petitioner got admitted at Saroj Hospital, from where, he was discharged on 14.09.2014.

Perusal of the record further reveals that thereafter also, the treatment of the petitioner continued as an out-patient at Saroj Hospital and his last prescription was dated 27.10.2014 and on the said date, he was declared fit to join light duty.

"6.4 The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, education and other factors.

6.5. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps:
(i) The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
(ii) The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

(iii) The third step is to find out whether :
a) The claimant is totally disabled, earning any kind of livelihood, or b) Whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or c) Whether he was prevented all restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
